claims.text: A framework combining ab initio phonon calculations with machine learning will accurately rank and identify single-phase high-entropy alloys with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity.
The integrated framework will outperform conventional average-parameter-based thermal-conductivity models.
Severe atomic disorder produces complex phonon-scattering mechanisms that conventional averaging models do not adequately capture.
The target materials are homogeneous, single-phase HEAs containing five or more principal elements and exhibiting lattice distortion and chemical disorder.
Ab initio calculations can supply detailed phonon dispersions and force-constant fluctuation metrics for use by the machine-learning model.
Elemental mass variance, bond-strength variation, and lattice-distortion parameters are predictive features for HEA lattice thermal conductivity.
The predictions are intended to apply under equilibrium conditions at room and elevated temperatures.
XRD can establish phase purity, laser-flash analysis can be used to derive lattice thermal conductivity, and inelastic neutron scattering can characterize phonon dispersion for validation.
Severe lattice distortion enhances phonon scattering and reduces phonon mean free path.
Fluctuations in local force constants enhance phonon scattering and reduce phonon mean free path.
Enhanced phonon scattering reduces lattice thermal conductivity.
The integrated approach captures nonlinear effects of mass disorder and bonding disorder on phonon dynamics.
Explicitly modeling local lattice distortions and force-constant fluctuations will yield lower intrinsic lattice-conductivity estimates than traditional averaging methods.
HEAs can exhibit very low lattice thermal conductivity because lattice distortion reduces phonon velocity and enhances phonon scattering.
Candidates selected by the framework will have lattice thermal conductivity approximately 20–50% below conventional-model predictions.
The framework is applicable only to single-phase, well-mixed HEAs with significant configurational entropy and uniform lattice distortions.
The framework may not be effective in multiphase alloys or systems whose thermal transport is dominated by secondary phases.
Detailed experimental thermal-conductivity benchmarks remain limited for many HEAs.
